title: A new commandment (John 13:34–35)
hookLine: love one another as I have loved you; by this all will know

lines: JUDAS GOES OUT INTO THE NIGHT.
cards: How do you spot a team's fans in an airport? The jersey. A nurse?
The scrubs, the clip-on badge. A soldier, a chef, a judge: there's usually something you can see. Uniforms answer the question, who are you with?
Judas has just gone out into the night, John says. And Jesus, with the eleven who are left, tells them how people will be able to pick them out of a crowd. It isn't a uniform.

teach.h: NOT NEW: LEVITICUS ALREADY SAID IT.
teach.b: Here are the words, in the Douay-Rheims: "A new commandment I give unto you: That you love one another, as I have loved you, that you also love one another. By this shall all men know that you are my disciples, if you have love one for another."

What's new about it? Love of neighbor is already in Leviticus: thou shalt love thy friend as thyself, as the Douay renders it, and Jesus quotes it himself in the other Gospels. The new part is the measure.

teach.h: NEW: AS I HAVE LOVED YOU.
teach.b: Not as you love yourself, but as I have loved you. And how has he loved them? An hour ago he was on his knees with a towel, washing their feet.
Within a day he'll lay down his life.
Then the sign: all men will know. Not by a creed recited, or a building, or a badge, but by something people can watch from outside: how these people treat each other.
Around the year 200, the North African writer Tertullian reported how outsiders talked about Christians in his city: look how they love one another, and how ready they are to die for each other.
The Latin for commandment is mandatum, and that word gave Holy Thursday its old English name, Maundy Thursday.
On that night, as the priest washes feet, the Church traditionally sings an antiphon that begins, in Latin, mandatum novum: a new commandment.

how: At the Holy Thursday Mass of the Lord's Supper, the Church sings antiphons during the washing of feet, traditionally including one drawn from John 13:34, "Mandatum novum," a new commandment.

games.q: you're one of the eleven. Judas has just left. Jesus says people will be able to tell you're his disciples. how?
o: by the words of your prayers.
by the way you love one another.
games.why: by this shall all men know that you are my disciples, if you have love one for another.

practice: Bring to mind the people you'll actually see today, at home, at work, at school, in a group chat, and pick one.
Think of one thing you could do for them that someone else might notice, standing up for them, a public thank you, sitting with the person nobody sits with, and picture yourself doing it.
If you pray, hold the line, as I have loved you; if not, just hold that one person.

wordCard.voice: Mandatum. The Latin for commandment, the root of Maundy Thursday: love one another as Jesus loved them, with a towel and a cross. Today's word.
